title: Localized, unstable, and entangled: Exploring ‘Us vs. Them’ bias in Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring behavioral asymmetry by performing sentiment analysis on next-token predictions and 30-token continuations using the LabMT lexicon, specifically comparing prompts framed with ingroup pronouns ('we'/'us') against matched prompts framed with outgroup pronouns ('they'/'them').

bias_targets.target: Social identity bias (including Gender, Racial, Religious, Political, and Socioeconomic biases)
bias_targets.methodology: Applying the 'us-vs.-them' sentiment framing evaluation across a controlled dataset of 660 prompts covering 165 persona traits across 16 distinct demographic and social domains, and analyzing the internal representations using Edge Attribution Patching (EAP).
